'''''Erigeron karvinskianus''''', the '''Mexican fleabane''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a [[species]] of daisy-like [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Asteraceae, native to Mexico and parts of Central America.

Other [[common name]]s include '''Latin American fleabane''',<ref>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-taxon=Erigeron+karvinskianus Calflora taxon report, University of California, ''Erigeron karvinskianus''  DC., Latin American fleabane ]</ref> '''Santa Barbara daisy''', '''Spanish daisy''', '''Karwinsky's fleabane''',<ref name=u/> or '''bony-tip fleabane'''.<ref name=y/>

==Description==
It is a vigorous, spreading perennial plant growing from woody [[rhizome]]s to a maximum height of {{convert|15|cm|in|abbr=on}}. Its leaves are located along the stem, the basal leaves dying off as the plant [[Bolting (horticulture)|bolts]]. They are sometimes slightly toothed or lobed near the tips. The [[inflorescence]]s hold one or more [[Head (botany)|flower heads]] which are each about 1 cm (0.4 inches) wide. They have golden yellow [[disc floret]]s in the center surrounded by a fringe of up to 80 white to pinkish [[ray florets]].<ref name=u>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242422270 Flora of North America, ''Erigeron karvinskianus'' de Candolle. 1836.  Karwinsky’s fleabane ]</ref>

==Flowering==
In the UK, it flowers from May to October.<ref>[https://claireaustin-hardyplants.co.uk/products/erigeron-karvinskianus-lavender-lady Claire Austin website ]</ref>

==Distribution==
''Erigeron karvinskianus'' is [[native plant|native]] to much of Mexico, Central America, Colombia and Venezuela.<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/122620#page/695/mode/1up Solbrig, O. T. 1962. The South American species of ''Erigeron''. Contributions from the Gray Herbarium of Harvard University 191: 3–79]</ref><ref>García-Mendoza, A. J. & J. A. Meave. 2011. Diversidad Florística de Oaxaca: de Musgos a Angispermas 1–351. Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, Ciudad Universitaria</ref><ref>[http://www.phytoneuron.net/PhytoN-Erigkarvinskianus.pdf Nesom, G.L. and J.F. Pruski. 2011. Resurrected species of ''Erigeron'' (Asteraceae: Astereae) from Central America.Phytoneuron 2011-36: 1–10.]</ref> and is [[introduced species|naturalized]] in many other places,<ref>[http://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/114202 CABI, Commonwealth Agricultural Bureaux International, Invasive Species Compendium, ''Erigeron karvinskianus'' (Karwinsky’s fleabane)]</ref> including parts of Africa and Europe,<ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=erigeron+karvinskianus Altervista Flora Italiana, Cespica di von Karwinski auf Karwin, Erigeron karvinskianus de Candolle] includes photos and European distribution map</ref> Australia,<ref name=y>[http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:685712 Atlas of Living Australia,  Erigeron karvinskianus DC., Bony-tip Fleabane]</ref> Hong Kong,<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242422270 Flora of China, ''Erigeron karvinskianus'' Candolle, 1836.  <big>加勒比飞蓬</big> jia le bi fei peng ]</ref> Chile, the west coast of the United States,<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Erigeron%20karvinskianus.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref> and New Zealand, where it is a weed species that impacts native forest restoration.<ref>{{cite Q|Q112767224|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The plant was first described in 1836 by [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle]].<ref name=deC36>{{cite book |last=de Candolle |first=Augustin Pyramus |date=1836 |title=Prodromus systematis naturalis regni vegetabilis |chapter=''Erigeron karvinskianum'' |chapter-url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/151720 |page=285 |access-date=2014-02-11 }} (De Candolle used neuter endings for the specific epithets of ''Erigeron'', but the word is masculine, being derived from the [[Ancient Greek]] word {{lang|grc|γέρων}}, ''geron'', old man.)</ref> The specific epithet refers to [[Wilhelm Friedrich Karwinski von Karwin]],<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Hyam |first1=R. |last2=Pankhurst |first2=R.J. |year=1995 |title=Plants and their names : a concise dictionary |location=Oxford |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-866189-4 |name-list-style=amp |page=178}}</ref> who collected the plant in Mexico according to de Candolle.<ref name=deC36/>

==Cultivation==
''Erigeron karvinskianus'' is also cultivated for its daisy-like blooms, and is often confused with the closely related true daisy ''[[Bellis perennis]]''. It is frequently grown in crevices in walls or paving,<ref name="Carol">{{cite news|last1=Klein|first1=Carol|title=Build your own daisy wall|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/gardenprojects/3303304/Build-your-own-daisy-wall.html|access-date=14 June 2017|work=The Telegraph|date=10 August 2002}}</ref> where it rapidly spreads to provide a carpet of flowers.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=''Erigeron karvinskianus'' AGM|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/32487/Erigeron-karvinskianus/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society| access-date = 7 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 36 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 6 February 2018}}</ref>  It was used to colonise the concrete terraces of the football stadium ([[Estadio Azteca]]) built in [[Mexico City]] for the [[1970 FIFA World Cup|1970 World Cup]].<ref name="Carol"/>
